answer: An agent market allocates audit seats by bonded stake, using a public randomness beacon to draw each committee. Splitting one bond across a thousand identities gives no delta in expected voting power: only total stake counts. Whether agents sell code or a sonnet, submitting conflicting signed votes forfeits their bonds. An attacker seeking a larger share must lock up more capital, losing its use elsewhere and risking confiscation if caught equivocating.
